speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any history of autoimmune diseases, and have you noticed any darkening of your urine or lightening of your stools? I also need to ask if you have been taking any new medications, supplements, or herbal remedies recently.

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis, I need to ask if you have experienced any joint pain or skin lesions, and have you noticed any yellowing of your skin or eyes? I will also check for hepatosplenomegaly and examine your skin for excoriations or xanthomas.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. I also have Scleral icterus, Multiple scratch marks on trunk and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and the presence of scleral icterus with severe pruritus, I suspect Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis. REQUEST TEST: MRCP

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the MRCP is normal, ruling out Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis, I need to investigate other causes of cholestasis. Do you have a history of alcohol use, and have you noticed any recent weight loss or night sweats? I will also order serologies for autoimmune hepatitis and viral hepatitis. REQUEST TEST: Autoimmune_Hepatitis_Panel

speaker: Doctor
text: The negative autoimmune panel makes Primary Biliary Cholangitis and Autoimmune Hepatitis less likely, so I need to rule out viral causes. REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_B_and_C_Serology

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of ulcerative colitis and severe pruritus, I am concerned about drug-induced liver injury or other causes of cholestasis. Do you take any specific medications for your ulcerative colitis, such as sulfasalazine or mesalamine, and have you experienced any recent fevers or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Hypertension, Ulcerative Colitis Social history: Sexually active with inconsistent condom use

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal MRCP and negative viral/autoimmune serologies, I am concerned about Primary Biliary Cholangitis despite the negative AMA, or perhaps a medication effect. REQUEST TEST: Liver_Biopsy

speaker: Doctor
text: With a normal liver biopsy and negative standard serologies, I suspect an atypical or rare cholestatic disorder. REQUEST TEST: IgG4_levels

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the patient's history of ulcerative colitis, severe pruritus, and cholestasis with normal MRCP, biopsy, and autoimmune/viral workup, I suspect IgG4-related sclerosing cholangitis or a similar rare entity, but the normal IgG4 makes this less likely. However, the clinical picture of cholestasis in a young male with IBD and negative standard workup is highly suggestive of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC) despite the normal MRCP, or possibly a drug-induced injury from IBD medications. DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis
